title: Batch Updates of Distributed Streaming Graphs using Linear Algebra
problem: Efficiently performing batch updates (vertex and edge additions/removals) on streaming graphs in distributed-memory parallel systems while minimizing inter-process communication overhead.
motivation: Streaming graphs with continuous updates require efficient distributed algorithms that scale to large supercomputing systems.
method: The algorithm stores graphs as distributed sparse matrices—number grids stored across multiple computers where most positions contain zero. When you add or remove a batch of vertices or edges, the algorithm converts these updates into mathematical matrix operations instead of requiring computers to pass messages to each other. It reduces communication overhead through carefully designed algorithms and shared-memory parallelism (where multiple processors within a single computer access shared data without messaging), and it maintains balanced workload across computers by rearranging the matrix's rows and columns during updates.
key_novelty: The core insight is that graph batch updates can be framed as mathematical operations on sparse matrices, which inherently reduces communication between computers and keeps work balanced through matrix rearrangement.
contributions: Distributed-memory parallel algorithm for streaming graph batch updates using sparse matrix operations
Communication reduction strategy through linear-algebraic reformulation of graph updates
Load balancing technique via matrix permutation during batch updates
Demonstration of 25x speedup over alternative linear-algebraic methods with linear scaling to 4,096 cores
primary_theme: distributed sparse matrix operations for streaming graph updates
